{{Top}}
{{Quote|There are so many! Do they all have a system of planets?|A nine year-old Anakin Skywalker, looking at the stars|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
[[File:Red_Star.jpg|thumb|right|220px|A red star]]
A '''star''' was an enormous sphere producing heat and light (in essence, it was a giant ball of [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]]). [[Star system/Legends|Systems]] of [[Planet/Legends|planets]] would usually form around stars when the gas and dust around them became stable enough. Stars could come in all sorts of sizes, [[Color/Legends|colors]], and temperatures. Most planets were seen orbiting medium mass orange-yellow stars, often called '''suns'''.

Stars visibility was measured in magnitudes. An [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Class Star Destroyer]] was undetectable against the background of a first-magnitude star, even with the best instruments.<ref name="Tyrant">''[[Tyrant's Test]]''</ref>

It was estimated that there were four hundred billion stars in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. There were 7.1 billion habitable stars in the known galaxy, which made up about 3.2 billion habitable star systems. This means that many systems contained two or more stars.<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Red dwarfs accounted for approximately 70 percent of the galaxy's stars.<ref name="Endor and the Moddell Sector">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Traveling through hyperspace ain't like dusting crops, boy! Without precise calculations we could fly right through a star or bounce too close to a supernova, and that'd end your trip real quick, wouldn't it?|Han Solo, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
The parts of a star located above its surface were collectively referred to as the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. They comprised two principal zones: the chromosphere and the corona. The chromosphere was a gaseous, relatively cool layer located immediately above the surface, and the corona was the tenuous, rarefied gaseous outermost part of the atmosphere.<ref name="SW58">[[Star Wars (1977) 58|''Star Wars'' (1977) 58]]</ref>

==Types of stars==
{{Quote|It's rare for a star to have even one planet that people can live on, but it's even rarer for a star to have more than one.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="AaC">''[[Ambush at Corellia]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Sequence_stars.png|300px|thumb|Comparison of star types]]
There were seven types of '''main sequence''' stars in the galaxy:<ref name="Atlas" />

*"'''O'''" stars were blue and hot, and had a lifespan of less than one million years. There were approximately one hundred million habitable O stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Garnib (star)/Legends|Garnib]].

*"'''B'''" stars were white-blue and hot, and had a lifespan of ten million years. There were approximately one hundred million habitable B stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Kessa/Legends|Kessa]].

*"'''A'''" stars were white and hot, and had a lifespan of four hundred million to two billion years. There were approximately one hundred million habitable A stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Colu/Legends|Colu]].

*"'''F'''" stars were yellow-white and medium-temperature, and had a lifespan of four billion years. There were approximately one hundred million habitable F stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Ropagi/Legends|Ropagi]].

*"'''G'''" stars were yellow and medium-temperature, and had a lifespan of ten billion years. There were approximately two billion habitable G stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Corell/Legends|Corell]].

*"'''K'''" stars were orange and cool, and had a lifespan of sixty billion years. There were approximately 3.75 billion habitable K stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Yavin/Legends|Yavin]].

*"'''M'''" stars were red and cool, and had a lifespan of approximately one hundred trillion years. They were also called '''red dwarfs'''. There were approximately seven hundred million habitable M stars in the galaxy. Example: [[Barab (star)/Legends|Barab]].

With O stars being the biggest in the sequence, the size decreased gradually to the smallest M stars.
[[File:Tatooine3.png|thumb|right|200px|[[Tatoo I/Legends|Tatoo I]] and [[Tatoo II/Legends|Tatoo II]], twin suns of the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]].]]
In addition to the main sequence stars, 10 percent of all stars in the galaxy were non-main sequence, of which five hundred million were habitable.<br />
The non-main sequence stars include:<ref name="Atlas" />

'''Pre-main sequence''' (smaller than M stars):
*[[Brown dwarf/Legends|Brown dwarf]]. Example: [[Doornik-1142/Legends|Doornik-1142]].
*[[Protostar/Legends|Protostar]]. Example: [[Black Bantha Nebula/Legends|Black Bantha]].
'''Post main-sequence''' (bigger than O stars):
*[[Red giant/Legends|Red giant]]. Example: [[Sokor/Legends|Sokor]].
*[[Blue giant/Legends|Blue giant]]. Example: [[Ku'Bakai]].
*[[Red supergiant/Legends|Red supergiant]]. Example: [[Primus Goluud/Legends|Primus Goluud]].

'''Compact stars''':
*[[White dwarf/Legends|White dwarf]]. Example: [[Ardos/Legends|Ardos]].
*[[Black dwarf/Legends|Black dwarf]]. Example: [[The Ring/Legends|The Ring]].
*[[Neutron star/Legends|Neutron star]]. Example: [[Din Pulsar/Legends|Din Pulsar]].
*[[Black hole/Legends|Black hole]]. Example: [[Maw Cluster/Legends|The Maw]].

Other exotic star types existed that did not fit precisely into this system of classification. These included [[Verde system/Legends|the star]] of the [[Verde system/Legends|Verde system]], considered a blue dwarf,<ref name="Secrets">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> and [[Ka'Dedus]], classified as an ultraviolet supergiant.<ref name="TPOC">''[[The Politics of Contraband]]''</ref> [[Black hole/Legends|Black holes]] were referred to as class "P" stars.<ref name="Atlas" />

==Behind the scenes==
The OBAFGKM sequence is the [[Wikipedia:Stellar_classification|same classification system]] used for identifying stars from Earth. However, in terms of Earth astrophysics, certain descriptions of stars in the Galaxy Far Far Away are shaky. Scientific bloopers abound such as blue supergiants that exist for long enough for a sentient species to evolve, inexplicably large brown dwarfs or red giants that are stable enough to house a habitable planet. The existence of black dwarfs is also impossible, as the universe is only about [[13,000,000,000 BBY|thirteen billion years old]],<ref name="Atlas" /> and those take trillions of years to form.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://spiff.rit.edu/classes/phys230/lectures/planneb/planneb.html|text="Late stages of evolution for low-mass stars"|author=Michael Richmond|archivedate=20200917075128}}</ref>
